newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's ACCC okays Air NZ Jetset buy.
newsitem.headline: Australia's ACCC okays Air NZ Jetset buy.

text.p: Australia's anti-monopoly body, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), said on Friday it would not oppose the proposed acquisition by Air New Zealand Ltd of a further 50 percent stake in Jetset Travel and Technology Holdings Pty Ltd.
"The ACCC has concluded that the proposed acquisition is unlikely to substantially lessen competition," ACCC chairman Allan Fels said.
Jetset is a retail travel agent, tour wholesaler and a consolidator of airline tickets to retail agents.
Jetset has preferred supplier arrangements with both Ansett Airlines and Qantas Airways Ltd, Fels said in a statemennt.
"The ACCC expects that Air NZ will maintain both these arrangements," he said.
Jetset was founded by Australian businessman Isi Leibler and Air NZ became a 50 percent shareholder in 1985.
The company has an annual turnover of more than A$1 billion, Air NZ said when announcing the proposed purchase on June 19.
